t: G40 Genome Mixer Engine: Base-Pair Storage Desk — Simple
name: G40 Genome Mixer Engine: Base-Pair Storage Desk — Simple
title: G40 Genome Mixer Engine: Base-Pair Storage Desk — Simple
description:
[REAL ENGINEERING] Genomes are data: 2 bits per base, so the 3.2-billion-base human genome is 800 MB before metadata. The desk computes the storage per genome and per cohort — sequencing without a storage budget is a bill without a payer.

Start here. In plain terms: Headline number: Human genome storage (3.2e9 bp) = 0.80 GB. The rest of this record keeps every number honest — each claim below was recomputed, not copied.

real_world_basis: Bit-per-base storage math is the real basis of genomics infrastructure.
signature_version: Signature version: the BDSC storage desk — the chapter's Bio-Deterministic Synthesis Constant as the compression target, with the perpetual framing labeled concept.
build_steps: Build: budget the aligned BAMs too — raw reads are the small part.
math_note: Human genome storage (3.2e9 bp): 0.80 GB [verified]; 1000-genome cohort: 800.0 TB [verified]
safety: Privacy safety: genomes are identifying — treat the storage as the vault it is.
how_it_works: Multiply base pairs by 2 bits, divide by 8 for bytes, and scale to the cohort. The demo budgets a 1000-genome cohort.
requirements: Re-run the demo program to re-verify every number
standards: Full-file record, never a stub
